messages.author: af25fc7ce08ea1c7
messages.subject: Combination of stacking and dodging
parts:
Hi @all :-),

I recently search for a beautiful solution to display stacked bars
(for a certain variable) in a bar-chart side by side for different
groups (dodges).
My task is to show the comparison of a variable of one type of subject
compared with the values of all types of subjects (the compared
included) together.
The first approach was to solve it with facets. I considered that as
pretty nice, on the upper half of the window you can see the overall-
rates and on the lower half the evaluation of only one subject. But
the customer is not satisfied with that solution (though it is an
uncommercial project :-D). All in all, what I need is a combination of
the "position=stack" and "position=dodge" functionality. Hadley, I
have read a discussion between you and another user, who got exactly
the same question. But that was on october 25th 2008. Maybe there is
an easier solution for it now ? I see, that I could easily solve it
with aes(x=as.numeric(variable) + *shifting*)). But is there an
approach integrated in the proper use of ggplot2 ? Some new parameter
for facetting ? Excuse me, if I oversaw that fact in the ggplot2 -
book. What I am searching for is simply stack-dodging :-).

Sorry, if I stole your time.

Best Regards,

Edgar

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Combination of stacking and dodging
parts:
Hi Ed,

Currently, there's no way to combine stacking and dodging in a single
layer (and I'm not sure even how it could work, in terms of separating
which elements should be grouped and which should be dodged).

In the future, I think you'll be able to do what you want with
faceting, because you'll be able to put the labels on the bottom of
the plot, and format them so they look like regular labels. Hopefully
that will be easy after I've rewritten the layout code this summer.

Hadley
